newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares surge, ease seen on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares surge, ease seen on profit-taking.

text.p: Leading Russian shares followed U.S. blue chips higher in early trade on domestic speculation and Western portfolio building before a market holiday, but traders saw levels easing on profit-taking by market close.

"Some people are trying to push the market up and ...sell higher later today. I think the market may end lower -- not lower than yesterday, but lower than the high point today," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze.
The Russian Trading System of 22 shares opened at 306.23 after closing at 305.53 on Tuesday.
But traders said Western and domestic demand in the wake of the Dow Jones 179-point rise and before a four-day holiday starting on Thursday was driving prices up in early trade.

"There's interest not just from Russian players but also Western," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Oleg Martynenko. "Everyone is taking a position before the holidays. I think (the Dow Jones rise) played a role although it is not a direct link."
National power utility UES jumped to $0.2550 at 0820 GMT but later eased to $0.2515 after closing on Tuesday at $0.2380.
Regional power company Mosenergo rose to $1.330 at 0835 GMT from $1.292.
"We're rolling here, shares have broken through all the resistance levels and UES hit an all time high -- the market is growing," said ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko.
Chkikvadze said Kubanelektrosvyaz, Chelyabinsk Svyazinform and Samara Svyazinform on the second tier RTS-2 market were also in demand.
The Dow industrial index registered its second-largest point rise in a single day on Tuesday at just short of the all-time record gain of 186.84 points on October 21, 1987.

Western analysts said strong corporate earnings reports and data released on Tuesday showing lower-than-expected U.S. wage inflation and orders for manufactured goods helped to power the surge and said the U.S. market would likely continue to gain.
Consumer price inflation figures released a few weeks ago fuelled investor fears of another interest rate hike coming out of the Federal Reserve's next meeting on May 20.
The Fed raised short-term rates by 25 basis points on March 25, driving money out of Wall St. and pulling the Dow down 10 percent.
A report on US first-quarter gross domestic product due out later on Wednesday could help the market if it was positive, Russian dealers said.
But they said a sustained rise in market levels widely predicted for May or early June had not yet started.
"I think this is the presentiment of it. People are starting to feel that it will happen and are taking their positions," said Martynenko.
